protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 1 of 3; refute not confirm; records host-effect-authorization.v8 as the accepted design contract
summary: Every axis the prompt names comes back clean, and the entry's central risk — that a coordinator recording gets mistaken for the owner recording that makes host acts exercisable — is refused in the decision text and again in the alternatives. Clause 2 states 'It is not FC-C1' and names what FC-C1 still requires; the corresponding alternative is rejected on the ground that v8's own fail-closed rule forbids it, which is true of v8's bytes. I verified the D-035 form claim against the adopted D-035 entry rather than accepting it, and D-038 follows that form on every element. All five input digests re-measure correct, including the Codex verdict, which I hashed without opening. One NOTE, on a cross-artifact state mismatch that D-038 cannot itself fix.

objections.claim: Adopting this entry would leave the corpus recording v8 as the accepted design contract while v8's own header still reads reviewStatus AWAITING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW.
objections.evidence: host-effect-authorization.v8.json at 2cbad5612e546d3bf915074a8ad3fc4cae444122c997e2ddb3fe067d3cd022dc carries status CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, sealRecommendation DO-NOT-SEAL, binds NOTHING, and reviewStatus AWAITING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW. Both independent reviews have now returned, so that last field is stale on its face. D-038 clause 1 records the artifact 'as the accepted host-effect design contract'. The mismatch is not D-038's error and it is not misstated by D-038: the pin-support line claims only 'v8 header (CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, binds NOTHING)', which is accurate and deliberately does not claim reviewStatus, and clause 5 forbids this entry from editing anything. It is also not trivially fixable, because correcting the field would produce a v9 whose digest is not the one this entry pins, which is a circularity rather than an oversight. I record it because this corpus has twice been bitten by stale cross-artifact state that nobody owned — the DR-011-R13 stale-D9 citation and the pin-move treadmill — and because a later reader encountering an adopted entry calling v8 accepted while v8 says it awaits review will have to reconstruct which is authoritative.
objections.proposedFix: Add one sentence to clause 1 or the readiness effect recording that v8's self-declared reviewStatus is stale by construction, that this recording rather than the artifact's own field is the standing statement of its review outcome, and that any v9 successor should carry the corrected field. That costs nothing and forecloses the reconstruction.

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 73957ee5d39e576afddbf0b58d4909eb49899beb7dcec3c37252546806cd7bdd both times. No drift.

The entry does not treat itself as FC-C1 owner recording, which is the axis that matters most. Clause 2: 'This recording is the D-035 analogue. It is not FC-C1. FC-C1 remains: Operability+security jointly with Security+platform must record a live instance. Coordinator recording of the accepted candidate is not that instance. Host acts stay unexercisable.' The alternative is rejected separately: 'Treat this recording as FC-C1. Rejected: v8's own fail-closed rule forbids it.' That rejection is true of v8's bytes — its FC-C1 conjunct reads that the contract must be recorded by those two owner groups and that 'This file existing is not that recording.'
Host acts do not become exercisable: clause 2 says so in terms, and nothing in the entry touches v8's six-conjunct fail-closed rule, which the entry cannot reach because clause 5 forbids editing.

No silent SATISFIED: the token occurs three times and all three are negative — clause 3's 'DR-105 and DR-114 stay OPEN. No SATISFIED', the rejected alternative 'Mark DR-105 or DR-114 SATISFIED. Rejected', and the readiness effect 'Zero. No SATISFIED. No blueprint.'

No join blocker waived: clause 4 states 'Join blockers BLK-1/2/3/4 remain STILL-ROUTED. This entry discharges none of them', which matches adopted D-032's disposition of those four and v8's own joinBlockerDisposition.

File 08 is not edited without MF-6: clause 5 states 'A later file-08 cell note that names this recording is a separate MF-6 act if it changes register content. This entry does not edit file 08.' That is the correct application of D-001 MF-6, which requires register-content changes to get their own D-000-reviewed entry and commit.

The D-035 form is not misstated. I read the adopted D-035 entry rather than accepting the claim. D-035 is 'RULE-GOVERNED recording of an independent ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES (0 blockers)', pins the subject and the verdict by digest, records that 'The row stays OPEN', states 'No freeze motion. No SATISFIED', gives a readiness effect of zero SATISFIED rows, and overturns by supersession plus revert. D-038 matches on every element: RULE-GOVERNED, subject and both verdicts pinned, rows stay OPEN, no SATISFIED, no freeze motion, readiness zero, overturn total. The one formal difference is presentational — D-035 carries a dedicated Verdict field while D-038 places both verdicts in the measured-inputs table — and the information is present either way.

The v8 verdicts are ACCEPT, so far as I can verify. My own verdict is pinned at 36a961e82a375778e71a08e7a66067843abb29a26170c84c38a12f15e121dec9, which matches my measurement, and it is ACCEPT with zero blockers and zero advisories, so clause 1's characterization of it is accurate. The Codex verdict is pinned at 3be46716fd7156e1b1ea23d4e2c5b55e16fafc8b834d824cedc3a8a66d15de93 and I confirmed that digest by hashing the file without opening it, preserving independence. I did not and cannot confirm that Codex's verdict is ACCEPT with zero blockers and zero advisories; that half of clause 1 is unverified by me and is recorded under whatIDidNotCheck.

All five measured inputs re-measure correct: v8 at 2cbad561, my verdict at 36a961e8, the Codex verdict at 3be46716, COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md at 7c6d8a56, and file 08 at 877e36d3. The last two are the current values, not stale snapshots.

D-000 clause 3 completeness, field by field: id, date, title, status, decision, alternatives (three, each with a reason), rationale carried by the decision-type basis line, decision type, reversibility class, overturn procedure, readiness effect. Reviewer verdict and commit land at adoption.

Examined and declined to raise: the reversibility class is a flat 'total' with no temporal boundary, where D-033 in the same dispatch carries one. I considered whether clause 5's later file-08 cell note is a dependent that would strand on revert. It is not, in the sense that matters — clause 5 makes any such note a separate MF-6 act with its own commit and its own revert, and adopted D-035, which this entry follows, likewise carries a flat overturn. Raising it here would move a standard I did not apply to D-035.
whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex review of D-038, and the Codex review of host-effect-authorization.v8. Neither read; the D-038 verdict file is confirmed absent at review time and the v8 verdict I hashed without opening. Clause 1's claim that Codex returned ACCEPT with zero blockers and zero advisories is therefore unverified by me. The digest is pinned, so a later reader can check it directly.
The merits of host-effect-authorization.v8. I reviewed it separately and accepted it; this entry records that outcome rather than reopening it.
Whether the owning authorities will record a live FC-C1 instance. That is the later act clause 2 preserves, and its non-performance is not a defect in these bytes.
Whether a file-08 cell note naming this recording should be written. Clause 5 correctly makes that a separate MF-6 act and takes no position on whether it happens.
D-033, reviewed separately in this session against the same prompt.

consentNote: I CONSENT on the merits with no MUST-FIX and no SHOULD-FIX. The entry does the one thing a recording entry must do and does it twice: it separates recording an accepted candidate from the owner act that would make host acts exercisable, in the decision text and again in the alternatives, and it grounds the refusal in v8's own fail-closed conjunct rather than in assertion. I verified the D-035 form claim against the adopted entry instead of accepting it, and it holds element by element. The single NOTE concerns a stale field in the artifact this entry records rather than anything the entry asserts, is not fixable inside this entry without circularity, and does not block adoption.
